sentences.text:
(Ramakant Vijaywargiya Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh ) Dated : 04-12-2025 Shri
Anil Khare - Senior Advocate with Shri Priyank Agrawal - Advocate for appellant.
Shri Manish Mukhraiya - Panel Lawyer for State.
Heard on admission.
Appeal, being arguable, is admitted for hearing.

Also heard on I.A. No.20368 of 2025, first application under Section 389 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to the appellant and I.A. No.20371 of 2025, an application for suspending the fine amount.

2. This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 06.08.2025 passed in Sessions Trial No.557 of 2021 by the learned Twenty-First Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal (M.P.), whereby present appellant has been convicted under Sections 420 (three counts) and 409 (three counts) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo five years R.I. and fine of Rs.25,000/- (on each count)
and seven years R.I. and fine of Rs.50,000/- (on each count) respectively with default stipulations.

3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that, as per the custody report dated 23.10.2025 the appellant has served four years, eleven months, and twenty-six days'
incarceration and as on today he has suffered more than five years incarceration, which amounts to more than half 2 CRA-8195-2025 of the total sentence awarded by the trial Court.
It is further submitted that the learned trial Court has awarded a sentence of seven years' rigorous imprisonment under Section 409 of the IPC.
It is further submitted that keeping in view the contradictions, omissions and variations in the statement of the witnesses, the present appellant has a good case on merits.
He is ready to comply with the condition as may be imposed by the Court.
It is also submitted that after admission, there is no likelihood of final hearing of this appeal in near future.
Therefore, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence of appellant be suspended and he be released on bail.

4. It is further submitted that the appellant is financially incapable of depositing such a substantial amount of fine particularly as he has been convicted in several other similar cases in which fines have also been imposed.
The appellant is 70 years old and has been incarcerated for a considerable period with no independent source of income.
In view of the aforesaid circumstances, a prayer has been made to suspend the fine amount.

5 . Per contra, learned counsel for the State has opposed the Ramakant Vijaywargiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51612965/
1 applications and prayed for its rejection.

sentences.text: 6. Having considered the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and after perusal of record, this Court is inclined to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant and released him on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on merits of the case, I.A. No.20368 of 2025 is hereby allowed a n d I.A. No.20371 of 2025 is hereby partly allowed.

Subject to depositing 50% of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond of Rs.70,000/- (Rupees Seventy Thousand Only) with a 3 CRA-8195-2025 solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.

The present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 23.03.2026 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE THK Ramakant Vijaywargiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51612965/
